newsitem.title: USA: U.S. invites Chilean president for state visit.
newsitem.headline: U.S. invites Chilean president for state visit.

text.p: President Bill Clinton has invited Chilean President Eduardo Frei for a state visit on Feb. 26, the White House announced on Thursday.

"This first state visit of (Clinton's) second term recognises our two governments' shared commitment to democracy and our rapidly expanding relationship with Chile," the White House said in a press statement.
The United States, together with Canada and Mexico, had offered Chile to open negotiations in 1994 to join the North American Free Trade Agreement.
Those talks, however, stalled in 1995 because the U.S. government failed to secure a "fast track" authority from Congress to close a deal.
After Clinton won re-election on Nov. 5, several U.S. officials have said that obtaining "fast track" will be a top priority for the White House.

"As a host of the next Summit of the Americas in March 1998, Chile will play a leading role in advancing our objective of building a hemispheric community of free-market democracies," the White House statement added.
In the first summit, held in Miami in 1994, 34 countries of the Western hemisphere agreed to work toward creating a Free Trade Area of the Americas by the year 2005.
